scope: Parts 14 through 31+ of the P5A milestone (Parts 1-13 were completed in prior sessions; this summary covers only the work performed to reach this final verdict).
production_mutation_confirmation: Every part of this milestone operated exclusively via read-only connections (PRAGMA query_only=1 / file:...?mode=ro) against database/flex_complete_database.db, database/wt_ops_v2.db, and database/local_operation_discovery_corpus.db. All writes throughout this milestone targeted ONLY: (a) database/_p5a_migration_build/ (the disposable candidate build, pre-existing from Parts 1-13), (b) /tmp/storage_p5a/ scratch files (outside the repo), (c) docs/audits/*.json artifacts, (d) docs/agent_handoff/current.json (a single additive, diff-checked, blockers-preserved update), and (e) a new pytest test file. No production database, table, or row was ever created, updated, or deleted.

eventual_physical_reclaim_estimate.caveat: Proportional estimate (COLD row-fraction applied to transfer_index's real dbstat-measured table+index bytes), not a direct post-deletion measurement -- P5A never deletes anything from production. A VACUUM would be required post-deletion to physically reclaim freed pages. See Part 28 for full methodology.

identity_reconciliation.method: Streaming chunked XOR-combined SHA256 digest over the composite key (signature, source, destination, amount_lamports, block_time)
identity_reconciliation.note: An initial attempt using raw `id` as the identity key produced a false-positive mismatch (cold segments use locally-renumbered ids, not global production ids) -- corrected and re-verified. See Part 15 artifact for the full investigation.

dedicated_transfer_graph_stats_endpoint_.note: Initial run flagged a HARD_STOP on the shared_funder_overlap_block sub-check; root-caused as a genuine SQL ORDER BY tie at the LIMIT 200 boundary with no secondary sort key (199/200 rows matched exactly; the 1 differing row on each side shared an identical tie value of 64) -- a query-determinism artifact, not lost or incorrect data. Verified via independent row-count/dedup check at the data layer (0 duplicate collapse) before accepting the corrected PASS verdict.

wallet_clustering_parity.method: Ran the ACTUAL WalletClusteringEngine._detect_dev_farms() production code (not a reimplementation) against production and a lean P5A-build test DB

three_sw2_parity.note: 3SW2's single known entity_address has no direct transfer_index rows within the frozen window on EITHER side -- a genuine 0/0 match, not a failure to find data. 3SW2's canonical evidence lives in wt_ops_v2.db operator_entities (untouched by P5A).

dv34_parity.discrepancy_summary: The prior-milestone '123' figure for Dv34's creator_funders population could not be reproduced against live production (which shows exactly 1 row today). Investigated and confirmed this is NOT a P5A artifact: (a) the P4 source of '123' was explicitly a SYNTHETIC FIXTURE, never a live measurement, and (b) creator_funders' single Dv34 row is byte-identical between production and the P5A build. P5A itself loses zero Dv34 evidence -- it faithfully reproduces whatever production's real current state is.

cex_lineage_parity.scope: 0/1/2-hop: PASS (5/5 real, previously-discovered on-chain signatures match exactly between production and the P5A build). 3-hop: NOT_TESTED (no independently-verified real 3-hop CEX-rooted chain found within a bounded search of the discovery corpus -- an absence-of-evidence, not a parity failure, since no chain that WAS found reconstructed differently).

discovery_parity.note: Every discovery-corpus-referenced signature (direct_funding_edges + upstream_edges) resolved identically on both sides, and lived entirely in HOT as expected (these signatures are a HOT pinning criterion by construction).

performance_benchmark.headline_finding: RECENT_ONLY 24h aggregate: 32.24s (production) vs 0.47s (P5A) -- a 68x speedup for the dominant real-world live-path query shape.
performance_benchmark.caveat: Not a clean engine-vs-engine comparison -- production queries ran against a live, concurrently-written 13.75GB file; P5A queries ran against a freshly-built in-memory table. Directionally real, not statistically hardened (single-run capture).

disk_safety: Never approached the 25 GiB caution threshold or 20 GiB hard-stop at any point in this milestone; lowest observed was ~39 GiB during the Part 19 test-DB build, immediately reclaimed to ~43 GiB after cleanup.

pre_existing_fk_condition_summary.status: CONFIRMED PRE_EXISTING_PRODUCTION_DATA_QUALITY_CONDITION, not a migration regression, out of scope for repair in this milestone

p5b_writer_quiesce_requirement.reason: The ONLY continuously-running process with a confirmed live write path into transfer_index (via realtime_creator_funding_extractor.extract_funding_for_new_token AND funder_incoming_extractor.extract_for_creator, both imported directly by pumpfun_curve_listener.py)
p5b_writer_quiesce_requirement.blast_radius: Narrow -- a single supervisord program, not a whole-system freeze

expected_cutover_duration_estimate.estimated_final_quiesce_window: Seconds, not minutes, provided pre-cutover delta-capture rounds are run frequently enough to keep the final gap small (projection based on measured per-row apply costs; not yet tested against a real quiesce since P5B is design-only).

rollback_design_summary.procedure: rm -rf database/_p5a_migration_build/ -- safe and complete because the entire candidate build is a read-derived copy that production has zero dependency on; no production restore or schema reversion is ever needed since nothing was migrated INTO production.
rollback_design_summary.audit_trail_preserved: All docs/audits/storage_lifecycle_p5a_part*.json artifacts remain in git history regardless of whether the physical build directory is deleted.

gitignore_flag.issue: database/_p5a_migration_build/replacement_main.db IS covered by the existing '*.db' gitignore rule, but database/_p5a_migration_build/cold_segments/*.sqlite (41 files, ~1GB) is NOT covered by any existing rule (no '*.sqlite' pattern exists in .gitignore).
gitignore_flag.action_taken: Per instruction, did NOT add a new gitignore rule unilaterally -- flagged here instead. Mitigated by committing only explicitly-named files (never `git add -A` or `git add .`) so this gap could not cause an accidental commit in this session.
gitignore_flag.recommendation_for_human: Consider adding a 'database/_p5a_migration_build/' directory-level gitignore rule (or a '*.sqlite' pattern) to close this gap for future sessions.

tests_added.coverage: Identity-reconciliation XOR-digest math (determinism, order-independence, partition-independence, the specific v1-bug regression with locally-renumbered ids), and the segment_name_for_month() discovery-index logic at a synthetic 41-segment scale mirroring the real Part 27 finding. All isolated tmp_path/in-memory fixtures, no real database touched.
